suppress.notes: False positive — wrong product. CVE-2022-31691 (CVSS 9.8) is an RCE in the YAML editing support of *Spring Tools 4 for Eclipse* (<= 4.16.0) and the related VSCode extensions (Spring Boot Tools, Concourse CI Pipeline Editor, Bosh Editor, Cloudfoundry Manifest YML Support). It has nothing to do with the `spring-boot-devtools` library; Dependency-Check matches it on the shared `vmware:spring_boot` CPE. Independently, devtools is declared `developmentOnly`, so it is never packaged into a deployable artifact. Re-evaluate if a CVE is ever published against the devtools library itself.

False positive — version out of range. CVE-2020-29582 is the Kotlin `createTempDir`/`createTempFile` information disclosure, which affects kotlin-stdlib <= 1.4.20 and was fixed in 1.4.21. Every JetBrains Kotlin artifact on any classpath here is well past that: the application resolves Kotlin 2.4.10, and the oldest straggler on a tool classpath is kotlin-reflect 1.6.10 (detekt's). Dependency-Check matches the JetBrains Kotlin CPE against artifacts whose own version strings it cannot map to a Kotlin release — the stdlib-jdk7/jdk8 shims, kotlin-reflect, and the coroutines builds. The pattern spans the whole `org.jetbrains.*kotlin(x)` family on purpose, including IntelliJ's repackaged `org.jetbrains.intellij.deps.kotlinx` coroutines: a narrower prefix let those through, and the reasoning applies identically to all of them. Re-evaluate only if this project ever downgrades below Kotlin 1.4.21.

False positive — wrong artifact. CVE-2026-34481 affects `org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-layout-template-json` (>= 2.14.0, < 2.25.4). That artifact is not on any classpath here; the only log4j artifacts present are log4j-api and log4j-to-slf4j (Spring Boot's SLF4J bridge), and both are already at 2.25.4. Dependency-Check matches on the shared `apache:log4j` CPE. Re-evaluate if log4j-layout-template-json is ever introduced.

False positive — wrong artifact within the same CVE. CVE-2026-49844 is a MapMessage JSON-serialization defect in `log4j-api` itself (2.13.1–2.25.4 and 2.26.0, fixed in 2.25.5 / 2.26.1). Dependency-Check additionally attributes it to `log4j-to-slf4j`, which merely bridges the Log4j API onto SLF4J and does not carry the affected code. NOTE: this suppression is deliberately scoped to log4j-to-slf4j ONLY. The finding against log4j-api is real — we resolve 2.25.4 — and is left visible on purpose until log4j is bumped to 2.25.5.

ACCEPTED RISK, NOT a false positive. CVE-2026-53914 genuinely affects JetBrains Kotlin < 2.4.20 and this project is on 2.4.10.
It is suppressed only because there is nothing to upgrade to: as of 2026-08-19 the newest build on Maven Central is 2.4.20-RC (checked against repo1.maven.org/.../kotlin-gradle-plugin/maven-metadata.xml — the sequence is Beta1, Beta2, RC, and no GA), and this project ships stable releases only. Upgrading is the preferred fix and should replace this entry the moment 2.4.20 is released. The progression Beta2 -> RC since this entry was written is the useful signal: GA is close, and the `until` date below was set with room for it.
The severity is disputed between the two scoring bodies: - NVD/NIST: 9.8 CRITICAL AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H - JetBrains (the CNA): 6.7 MEDIUM AV:L/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:L Dependency-Check uses the NVD score, so the finding trips failBuildOnCVSS = 7.0 and fails the enforced nightly scan. We accept the CNA's assessment as the better guide to real exposure here: JetBrains, as the vendor, scores it local-access, high attack complexity and high privileges required — an attacker already needs privileged local access to the build host, which is a materially different threat from the remote, unauthenticated vector NVD's 9.8 implies.
Scoped to the whole `org.jetbrains.*kotlin(x)` family because Dependency-Check attributes this CVE across ~22 of them (stdlib, reflect, compiler, scripting, build-tools, coroutines) from the single JetBrains Kotlin CPE. The pattern deliberately spans intermediate segments so it also covers IntelliJ's repackaged `org.jetbrains.intellij.deps.kotlinx` coroutines: the first version of this entry anchored on `org.jetbrains.(kotlin|kotlinx)/`, that one artifact slipped through, and it alone failed the enforced scan.
THE DEPENDABOT ALERT IS THIS ENTRY, NOT A SECOND FINDING (#266). GitHub raises it as GHSA-r937-wjx7-w2jp against org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-gradle-plugin from settings.gradle.kts, and that GHSA's own identifier list contains CVE-2026-53914 — one defect, two scanners, two views. GitHub's advisory carries the CNA's vector verbatim (6.7 MEDIUM, AV:L/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:L), so the GitHub half of the sweep and the reasoning above do not merely coexist, they agree; it is NVD that is the outlier. The alert is dismissed as `tolerable_risk` pointing here, so the two halves cannot drift into being triaged twice or accepted once and forgotten in the other place. Reopening it is one `gh api ... -f state=open` call if this reasoning stops holding.
REMOVAL: delete this entry when Kotlin 2.4.20 (or later) ships stable and is adopted — see the kotlin("jvm") version in settings.gradle.kts. The `until` date is a backstop, not a target: on 2026-11-05 the suppression lapses and the finding returns for re-evaluation whether or not anyone remembered to revisit it.
